talks.originalTitle: Self-Evolving Apps: Building Software That Gets Smarter Every Time You Use It

title.en: Self-Evolving Apps: Building Software That Gets Smarter Every Time You Use It
title.zh: 自进化应用：构建每次使用都会变得更智能的软件

talks.originalAbstract:
Most apps are built once and stay the same. Self-evolving apps are different, they improve every time you use them, not because someone updates the code, but because the app learns from your corrections.

This intelligence exists completely outside the app as a separate, updatable layer. Before each use, it reads your previous corrections and uses them as examples to make better decisions. No machine learning required, neither retraining or data science team. 

Drawn from several apps running in daily production, this talk shares what self-evolving apps are, how to design them, how to build one, which licensing models work best and the lessons I have learned from building several of these apps, as well as a live demonstration.

overview.en: Self-evolving apps improve with each use by learning from user corrections, not through code updates. This intelligence operates as a separate, updatable layer that uses past corrections to enhance decision-making without requiring machine learning or data science teams. The talk covers design, development, licensing models, and lessons learned from real-world applications.
overview.zh: 自进化应用通过学习用户的修正来不断改进，而不是通过代码更新。这种智能以独立可更新的层形式存在，利用过往修正提升决策能力，无需机器学习或数据科学团队。本次演讲将介绍自进化应用的设计、开发、授权模式及实际应用中的经验教训。

talks.originalTitle: Network-Sourced AI: Open Ensembles, Private Data, and a Reproducible Path to the Frontier

title.en: Network-Sourced AI: Open Ensembles, Private Data, and a Reproducible Path to the Frontier
title.zh: 网络源生 AI：开放集成、私有数据与通往前沿的可复现路径

talks.originalAbstract: Frontier AI has become concentrated in a handful of closed labs, and public benchmarks tell us little about how models actually perform on real work — scores are frozen on publication day, easily gamed, and blind to the private, domain-specific data where the largest capability gains live. This talk presents "Network-Sourced AI," the open-source approach developed by the OpenMined Foundation to change that. Its foundation is multi-model ensembling: combining the answers of diverse models — open and closed, large and small — to systematically outperform any single model. On top of this, OpenMined applies Structured Transparency and attribution-based control, so every result is publicly reproducible and data owners retain full control over which evaluations remote models may perform on their data, protected by Privacy-Enhancing Technologies. I will show a demonstration of our newly launched open-source toolkit and public leaderboard, show how anyone can build, run, and reproduce state-of-the-art ensembles on their own machine using the AI subscriptions they already pay for, and discuss how data owners can turn private archives into community benchmarks without the data ever leaving their control.

overview.en: Network-Sourced AI, developed by the OpenMined Foundation, addresses the limitations of closed AI labs by using open ensembles of diverse models to improve performance. It combines Structured Transparency and Privacy-Enhancing Technologies to ensure reproducibility and data control. The talk demonstrates an open-source toolkit and public leaderboard, enabling users to build and reproduce state-of-the-art models locally while maintaining data privacy.
overview.zh: OpenMined基金会开发的Network-Sourced AI通过结合多种模型的开放集成，解决了封闭AI实验室的局限性。它采用结构化透明度和隐私增强技术，确保结果可复现且数据所有者能控制数据使用。演讲展示了新的开源工具包和公开排行榜，使用户能在本地使用已有AI订阅构建和复现最先进的模型，同时保持数据隐私。

talks.originalTitle: AI-Native Company Operating System: How Open Source Agents Transform Startup Workflows

title.en: AI-Native Company Operating System: How Open Source Agents Transform Startup Workflows
title.zh: AI 原生公司操作系统：开源智能体如何重塑初创企业工作流

talks.originalAbstract:
AI is not just changing how we build software — it is changing how companies are organized.

Traditional organizations are built around human roles, processes, and software tools. AI-native organizations take a different approach: knowledge becomes structured memory, AI agents become collaborative workers, and workflows become intelligent systems that continuously learn and improve.

In this talk, Jacky Hsu, founder of Ingora and former Microsoft product leader, will share practical lessons from building an AI-native company developing Qrio, an AI learning companion for children and families.

The talk explores how a small startup team combines open-source technologies, AI agents, coding assistants, and knowledge systems to create an organization that can move from strategy and ideas to product design, engineering execution, and operational learning with unprecedented speed.
Rather than treating AI as isolated productivity tools, this session presents a vision of the company itself becoming an AI-powered operating system — where humans provide creativity, judgment, and vision, while AI agents amplify execution and organizational intelligence.

overview.en: AI is transforming how companies are organized, moving from traditional human-centric structures to AI-native systems where knowledge is structured memory and workflows become intelligent, self-improving systems. Jacky Hsu will discuss how Ingora leverages open-source agents, coding assistants, and knowledge systems to rapidly develop Qrio, an AI learning companion for children and families. This approach treats the company itself as an AI-powered operating system, enhancing execution and organizational intelligence through AI agents.
overview.zh: AI 正在改变企业的组织方式：企业正从传统、以人为中心的结构，转向把知识作为结构化记忆、把工作流构建为智能且持续改进的系统。Jacky Hsu 将分享 Ingora 如何利用开源智能体、编程助手和知识系统，快速开发面向儿童与家庭的 AI 学习伙伴 Qrio。这种方法把公司本身视为由 AI 驱动的操作系统，并通过智能体提升执行能力与组织智能。

talks.originalTitle: Your AI Product Is Ready. Is Your Company Ready for Europe?

title.en: Your AI Product Is Ready. Is Your Company Ready for Europe?
title.zh: 你的 AI 产品准备好了，你的公司准备好进入欧洲了吗？

talks.originalAbstract:
Europe represents one of the world's most attractive markets for AI companies. But for companies building and scaling AI products in Asia, entering Europe is no longer simply a question of finding customers, partners, or investors.
The European AI market is increasingly shaped by regulatory requirements, governance expectations, and new responsibilities for organisations developing, providing, deploying, or distributing AI systems.
For AI companies looking to expand internationally, the challenge is therefore not only to build a great AI product, but to understand whether the company, product, governance model, and operational processes are ready for the European market.
This session introduces a practical approach to EU AI Market Entry Readiness, exploring the key questions AI companies should address before scaling into Europe.
What is the regulatory status of your AI system? What role does your company play in the AI value chain? Could your system fall into a high-risk category? What governance, documentation, transparency, human oversight, and risk management requirements may apply? And what should companies consider before entering the European market rather than discovering regulatory challenges after they have already signed their first European customer?
The session will also explore how emerging technologies, including Agentic AI and increasingly autonomous systems, may create new governance and market-entry considerations.
The session will explore what European market entry really means for companies building AI outside Europe, and why regulatory readiness is becoming part of the journey, not an afterthought. The conversation will connect AI innovation, product strategy, governance, and international expansion, with a focus on the questions companies should be asking before they set their sights on the European market.
Because talking about regulation does not have to be boring. The goal is to challenge some common assumptions, bring a fresh perspective to the European AI market, and leave the audience thinking differently about what it really takes to take an AI product from Asia to Europe.

overview.en: Europe is a highly attractive market for AI companies, but entering it requires more than just a great product. Companies must ensure their governance, operations, and compliance are ready for Europe's regulatory environment. This session explores key questions AI firms should address before expanding into Europe, including regulatory status, risk categories, and governance requirements. It also discusses how emerging technologies like Agentic AI may influence market entry strategies and regulatory readiness.
overview.zh: 欧洲是AI公司极具吸引力的市场，但进入该市场不仅需要优秀的产品，还需要确保公司治理、运营和合规性符合欧洲的监管环境。本次演讲将探讨AI公司扩展至欧洲前应考虑的关键问题，包括监管状态、风险类别和治理要求。此外，还将讨论像Agentic AI等新兴技术如何影响市场进入策略和监管准备。

talks.originalTitle: Next-Generation System Interoperability: AI Agents as the Universal Integration Layer

title.en: Next-Generation System Interoperability: AI Agents as the Universal Integration Layer
title.zh: 下一代系统互操作性：AI 智能体成为通用集成层

talks.originalAbstract:

Rigid contracts, manual mappings, and brittle integrations struggle to keep up with the pace of change.

Agents can dynamically discover system capabilities, negotiate protocols, perform semantic translation, and orchestrate complex workflows — even between systems that were never designed to work together.

overview.en: Traditional interoperability methods like APIs and ESBs are struggling with today's dynamic and autonomous systems. This talk introduces agent-mediated interoperability, where AI agents dynamically discover, translate, and orchestrate system interactions, offering a flexible and universal integration solution.
overview.zh: 传统的方法如API和ESB在当今动态和自主的系统中已显不足。本次演讲提出了一种新的互操作性范式——智能体中介互操作性，通过AI 智能体动态发现、翻译和协调系统交互，提供一种灵活且通用的集成方案。

talks.originalTitle: The Sovereignty Layer: Why Open Source Is How the Global South Shapes AI

title.en: The Sovereignty Layer: Why Open Source Is How the Global South Shapes AI
title.zh: 主权层：为什么开源是全球南方塑造 AI 的方式

talks.originalAbstract:
The most powerful technology in human history is being shaped by a handful of companies, in a handful of cities, in a handful of languages. For most of humanity — women, the Global South, non-technical creators — the only role on offer is to consume what others decide. This is the defining risk of the AI era: not that machines will think, but that so few humans will hold the pen that writes our shared future.

Open source is the most powerful answer we have. But open weights and open code are necessary, not sufficient. If the people who use AI have no voice in how it's governed, "open" becomes a technical detail rather than a democratic reality. The missing layer isn't another framework — it's a structured way to turn millions of users into co-authors.

Drawing on my own path — born in Indonesia, the first and only Indonesian woman admitted to France's elite ENA (and only the third Indonesian ever), then a front-row witness to the launch of the current AI boom in Silicon Valley — I'll argue that open source and global participation are two halves of the same fight. One opens the technology; the other opens the decision.

I'll introduce the model behind Global AI Assembly and its three pillars: (1) Educate — short, hands-on AI training that turns non-technical people into builders, because you no longer need to be an engineer, you need to be curious; (2) Give Voice — structuring learners' real opinions, concerns, and needs into rigorous reports; and (3) Shape — carrying those citizen voices to governments, companies, and standards bodies so AI is built with people, not merely for them. With hubs from Paris to West Africa, this is open-source thinking applied not just to models, but to governance itself.

This talk is for the builders in the room who sense that the open-source movement is about more than performance benchmarks — that it is, at its heart, a fight over who gets to decide. I'll offer a concrete framework for how the open-source community can become the infrastructure of a genuinely democratic AI: sovereign, inclusive, and globally co-authored. Attendees will leave with a new lens on their own work — not as engineers optimizing a stack, but as architects of who the future belongs to. The question is no longer whether AI will change the world. It is: who holds the pen?

overview.en: The talk discusses how open source can empower the Global South in shaping AI governance. It introduces the Global AI Assembly model, which focuses on education, giving voice to users, and influencing AI development through structured participation. The speaker argues that open source is not just about code but about democratizing decision-making in AI.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨开源如何帮助全球南方参与塑造 AI 治理。演讲将介绍 Global AI Assembly 模式及其三大支柱：教育非技术人群、汇集用户声音，并通过结构化参与影响政府、企业和标准组织。演讲者认为，开源不只是开放代码与权重，更是让更多人共同参与 AI 决策的基础。

talks.originalTitle: Building a Knowledge-Work Harness: From Coding Agents to Executable Strategy

title.en: Building a Knowledge-Work Harness: From Coding Agents to Executable Strategy
title.zh: 构建知识工作 Harness：从编程智能体到可执行战略

talks.originalAbstract:
Coding harnesses work because code carries its own verifier: tests, compilers, type systems. An agent can run until something passes. Knowledge work has none of that — no compiler for a decision, no test suite for a strategy, and "done" is a judgment call. Building an agent harness for knowledge work is a vastly different problem than building one for code, and most of what the ecosystem has learned does not transfer cleanly.

This talk is a field report from a year of building and running one. I am a strategist, not a developer, and my one-person consultancy operates day to day on an open-source, local-first agent fleet: local models, flat-rate delegation, no cloud dependencies.

What the talk covers:

- Component by component, what survives the move from coding harness to knowledge-work harness — skills, memory, delegation, review gates — and what breaks. The verification gap is the organizing problem: what stands in for the test suite when the output is a decision.
- The layer that makes the harness work: strategy written as a protocol. Plain-text decision rules, closed schemas, and gates that both the human and the agents operate under — the firm's strategy as the harness's operating instructions, and the nearest thing knowledge work has to a verifier.
- Failure modes from daily production use: where plain text is enough, where it is not, and what a year of operation did to the strategy itself.

The talk includes a live demo: an agent reading the strategy files and making a gated decision, running locally on open-source infrastructure.

overview.en: Building a knowledge-work harness requires addressing the verification gap, as decisions lack the automated checks found in coding. This talk shares insights from a year of running an open-source, local-first agent system, focusing on components that survive the transition and the role of strategy as a protocol. A live demo illustrates an agent making a gated decision based on plain-text rules.
overview.zh: 构建知识工作框架需要解决验证缺口，因为决策缺乏代码中的自动检查。本次演讲分享了一年运行开源本地优先智能体系统的经验，探讨了组件迁移中的关键要素及策略作为协议的作用。演示展示了基于纯文本规则的智能体如何在本地基础设施上做出受控决策。

talks.originalTitle: Accelerating Algorithm Autoresearch

title.en: Accelerating Algorithm Autoresearch
title.zh: 加速算法自动研究

talks.originalAbstract:
Optimizing software has never been easier with the advent of agentic AI... right? It turns out it's not quite that simple!

Autoresearch is a powerful technique for optimization; an agent iteratively modifies, tests, and benchmarks changes to the codebase with the goal of maximizing the benchmark score.

While powerful, this process faces challenges, especially at scale:
- Cheating / reward hacking (just as in reinforcement learning).
- Overfitting to benchmark's inputs.
- Tradeoffs between input breadth and build/test/benchmark cost.
- Local maximums.

In this talk, we'll discuss some of these challenges and how to overcome them, based on examples from the open source GPUMODE kernel competitions and infrastructure.
We'll explore how to take autoresearch results from "cool idea" to "shipped in production".

overview.en: Optimizing software with agentic AI is more complex than it seems. Autoresearch, which uses agents to iteratively modify and test code, faces challenges like reward hacking and overfitting. This talk explores these issues and how to turn autoresearch results into production-ready solutions, using examples from open-source GPU kernel competitions and infrastructure.
overview.zh: 利用智能体 AI 优化软件比想象中复杂。Autoresearch 通过智能体迭代修改和测试代码，但面临奖励作弊（reward hacking）、过拟合等挑战。本次演讲将结合开源 GPU 内核竞赛和基础设施的实例，探讨这些问题以及如何将 Autoresearch 成果转化为生产可用的方案。

talks.originalTitle: Latest LF Research Reports on Agentic AI and AI Coding

title.en: Latest LF Research Reports on Agentic AI and AI Coding
title.zh: LF 最新智能体 AI 与 AI 编程研究报告

talks.originalAbstract: Report findings on the latest LF Research papers: 1) Enterprise Transitions to Agentic AI Era 2) Generative AI's impact on Open Source Software

It covers findings from two key papers: "Enterprise Transitions to Agentic AI Era" and "Generative AI's impact on Open Source Software." The reports highlight the evolving role of AI in enterprise systems and its influence on open source development.

talks.originalTitle: Agent-Centric Engineering — From Personal Productivity to Organizational Capability

title.en: Agent-Centric Engineering — From Personal Productivity to Organizational Capability
title.zh: 以智能体为中心的工程实践——从个人生产力到组织能力

talks.originalAbstract:
Talk Abstract: Agent-Centric Engineering — From Personal Productivity to Organizational Capability
Speaker: Dong Xin, Huawei Cangjie Programming Language Team
Former Microsoft Azure enterprise cloud expert and lead of Huawei's mobile AI tooling, Ascend MindStudio, HarmonyOS DevEco Studio, and the Cangjie/Bisheng C language IDE. Since early 2025, Dong Xin has pioneered AI Agent-driven R&D models and open-sourced ACEHarness, now adopted by multiple large-scale engineering teams.
The Shift: AI development has entered its second half. The challenge is no longer "coding faster alone," but how organizations restructure roles, redefine quality boundaries, and compose teams for Agent-centric workflows.
Three Pillars:
ACE (Agent-Centric Engineering): Engineers ascend from coders to Directors (orchestration), Screenwriters (specification), and Quality Arbiters (trust).
Human IO Loop: Human On the Loop for systemic control; Human In the Loop for result trust. Human attention focuses on objectives, boundaries, and risks—Agent executes autonomously.
ATM (Ability-based Task Matching): Dynamic task allocation to optimal executors.
The Cangjie Journey: From localized trials to organizational capability, with measurable gains in library development, crash analysis, documentation, API testing, and code review.
Two Battlefield Stories:
Compiler Memory Optimization (high-coupling): Pre-defined objectives and boundaries let the Agent autonomously design, implement, and self-repair—humans govern and accept at critical nodes.
Hash Library Performance (high-knowledge-density): A strike team of "Expert + Intern + Agent" delivered results while converting expertise into reusable knowledge assets.
ACEHarness: An open-source platform bridging team experience to engineering infrastructure—featuring Spec-Driven Development, state-machine workflows, intelligent Supervisor routing, adversarial iteration, multi-Agent deliberation, Git audit baselines, and long-term memory with skill extensibility.
Takeaway: A concrete framework for moving from AI tool adoption to Agent-centric organizational capability, with actionable patterns for human-AI governance and quality boundary definition.

overview.en: Agent-Centric Engineering (ACE) transforms individual productivity into organizational capability by redefining roles and workflows. Dong Xin introduced ACEHarness, an open-source platform enabling Spec-Driven Development and multi-Agent collaboration, with real-world applications in compiler optimization and hash library performance. The framework emphasizes human-AI governance and quality boundary definition for effective AI agent integration.
overview.zh: 以Agent为中心的工程（ACE）通过重新定义角色和工作流程，将个人生产力转化为组织能力。董鑫介绍了ACEHarness这一开源平台，支持基于规范的开发和多Agent协作，并在编译器优化和哈希库性能等实际应用中取得成效。该框架强调人机治理和质量边界定义，为AI 智能体集成提供可操作的模式。

talks.originalTitle: State of harness engineering

title.en: State of Harness Engineering
title.zh: Harness 工程现状

talks.originalAbstract: Coding agents are getting better fast, but many teams are discovering that better models and a pile of markdown instructions don't automatically mean they can lean back and reduce supervision. Harness engineering is the set of practices coding agent users have to shape how their agent behaves and how reliable its output is. Markdown instructions are part of it, but so are the controls and automated feedback loops built around the agent. This talk lays out a mental model for the harness engineering toolbox, then walks through the current landscape of practices, with a focus on giving agents feedback sensors.

overview.en: State of harness engineering explores the challenges of effectively managing coding agents. While models improve, teams find that better models alone aren't enough; they need structured practices to guide and refine agent behavior. The talk introduces a mental model for harness engineering, emphasizing feedback mechanisms and control systems to enhance reliability.
overview.zh: 本次演讲探讨了编程智能体的有效管理挑战。尽管模型性能不断提升，但团队发现仅依靠更强大的模型并不足够，还需系统性的实践来引导和优化智能体行为。演讲介绍了 harness engineering 的思维模型，重点强调反馈机制和控制系统以提升可靠性。

talks.originalTitle: AI时代网络安全的“矛”与“盾”

title.en: The “Spear” and “Shield” of Cybersecurity in the AI Era
title.zh: AI 时代网络安全的“矛”与“盾”

talks.originalAbstract:
我长期扎根于一线攻防实战，对AI如何重塑攻击链有切身体会。本次分享不空谈趋势，而是基于奇安信等一线安全公司的实战数据与最新案例，提供一套可落地、可复用的建设路径，希望能为现场的同仁提供真正的决策参考。
作为网络安全一线从业者，我深切感受到AI技术正在将网络攻防推向一个前所未有的“失衡”临界点。本次分享将结合近期发生的重大安全事件与前沿洞察，提出一套从战略到落地的“再平衡”解决方案，希望能与参会同仁共同探讨。
核心观点与内容大纲：
1. 警惕“工业化”攻击：Mythos与漏洞“军备竞赛”
我将首次在公开论坛深度剖析Anthropic旗下Mythos模型带来的范式级冲击。它实现了从漏洞挖掘到攻击执行的全自动流水线作业，将资深工程师数天的工作压缩至分钟级。这导致漏洞产出速度（分钟级）与补丁修复速度（平均72天）之间出现致命性“时差”，彻底打破了传统攻防博弈的平衡。
引用“玻璃翼计划”等案例，揭示当前攻击高效化、自动化、平民化的三大趋势，以及由此引发的全球关基领域系统性焦虑。
2. 防守“力不从心”：传统安全体系的三大崩溃
人的上限 vs AI的无限： 我们的人海战术、静态规则，在AI驱动的恶意代码变异、高频次攻击和全域扫描面前，已经形同虚设。
“内忧外患”加剧： 我将分享双重勒索、供应链攻击（如“DeepSeek”恶意包事件）、数据泄露（如科研机构违规用AI工具泄密） 等真实案例。这些案例无一不指向一个核心问题：安全孤岛化、单点化的防守体系，无法应对体系化、智能化的攻击。
3. 破局之道：从“追着漏洞跑”到“带着漏洞防”
核心观点：我们无法阻止漏洞被挖出，但可以重构防御体系，让攻击者“即使挖了洞，也打不进来，进得来也拿不走，拿走了也用不了”。
【三位一体】内生安全纵深防御体系： 我将详细阐述如何通过高位情报AI化、中位运营智能体化、低位产品MCP化，实现安全能力的协同联动。

4. 总结与展望：
网络安全已进入“体系对抗”时代。我们必须借鉴“社会治安综合治理”的网格化理念，通过一体化安全改造，让安全从“追着漏洞跑”的被动修补，转变为“带着漏洞防”的主动防御。
最终，安全不再是成本，而是数字化业务发展的底座和竞争力。

overview.en: Drawing on frontline cybersecurity experience, the speaker explains how AI is reshaping attack chains and presents a practical framework based on real-world data and cases from QI-ANXIN and other security companies. The talk examines the imbalance created by AI-driven attacks and proposes a "rebalance" strategy for moving from reactive patching to proactive defense.
overview.zh: 该演讲者长期参与一线攻防实战，分享AI如何重塑攻击链，并基于奇安信等公司实战数据提出可落地的建设路径。演讲聚焦AI引发的攻防失衡问题，提出从战略到落地的“再平衡”方案，旨在推动防御体系从被动修补转向主动防御。

talks.originalTitle: Mapping the Open Agentic AI Landscape: From Open Models to Cross-Foundation Architectures

title.en: Mapping the Open Agentic AI Landscape: From Open Models to Cross-Foundation Architectures
title.zh: 绘制开放智能体 AI 全景图：从开放模型到跨基金会架构

talks.originalAbstract:
As autonomous AI agents shift from experimental projects to production workloads, scaling them requires navigating a rapidly expanding open-source landscape. True technical sovereignty demands an open stack where transparent, open-weight models are backed by an open supply chain to establish verifiable trust. Managing multi-turn agentic loops requires seamless integration across open models, compute, orchestration, and agent protocols.

This landscape presentation maps the end-to-end open agentic ecosystem. At the substrate level, the PyTorch Foundation powers compute and model serving by hosting Ray for distributed execution alongside vLLM for high-throughput, memory-efficient serving. The CNCF delivers platform orchestration through Kubernetes, cloud-native agentic standards, and evolving AI Gateways that provide smart routing across a mixture of models while integrating agent harnesses directly into the platform. Finally, the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) standardizes tool execution and agent delegation via MCP and A2A specifications. 

Attendees will gain a comprehensive map of how these layers intersect to deliver a secure, sovereign alternative to proprietary AI stacks.

overview.en: The talk explores the open agentic AI landscape, emphasizing the need for transparent, open-weight models and an open supply chain to ensure technical sovereignty. It outlines the ecosystem, including PyTorch Foundation, CNCF, and AAIF, which together enable secure, scalable agentic systems through integrated compute, orchestration, and protocol standards.
overview.zh: 本次演讲梳理开放智能体 AI 的生态系统，强调透明度、开放权重模型和开放供应链对技术主权的重要性。演讲介绍 PyTorch 基金会、CNCF 和 AAIF 等生态组成部分，以及它们如何整合计算、编排和协议标准，共同支撑安全、可扩展的智能体系统。

talks.originalTitle: Teaching AI to Improve AI: From Experimental Feedback to Meta-Evolution

title.en: Teaching AI to Improve AI: From Experimental Feedback to Meta-Evolution
title.zh: 教 AI 改进 AI：从实验反馈到元进化

talks.originalAbstract:
Large language models are evolving from coding assistants into research agents that can propose solutions, run experiments, interpret feedback, and iteratively improve their results. Yet achieving a higher score in a single experiment does not mean that a system has truly learned how to improve.
This talk explores how execution-grounded experimentation can be transformed into reusable improvement capabilities. We first introduce the minimal AI4AI loop—propose, execute, evaluate, and revise—and distinguish one-off optimization from self-evolution, where experience changes the system’s future behavior. Through representative success and failure cases from NatureBench, we examine the key bottlenecks facing scientific agents, including method selection, implementation depth, and compute allocation. We then present Frontis-MA1 and OpenMLE, showing how executable tasks, structured feedback, evolutionary search, and post-training can be connected within a unified learning loop.
Finally, we return to recursive self-improvement: what would it take for an improved AI improver to take over the next improvement cycle and continually produce stronger successors?

overview.en: Large language models are evolving from coding assistants to research agents capable of proposing solutions, running experiments, and iteratively improving results. This talk discusses how execution-based experimentation can be transformed into reusable improvement capabilities, using the AI4AI loop and case studies from NatureBench. It also explores the potential for recursive self-improvement in AI systems.
overview.zh: 大型语言模型正从代码助手演变为能够提出解决方案、运行实验并迭代改进结果的研究智能体。本次演讲探讨了如何将基于执行的实验转化为可复用的改进能力，介绍了AI4AI循环和NatureBench中的案例研究。最后，还探讨了AI系统实现递归自我改进的潜力。

talks.originalTitle: KTransformers: The Fine-Tuning-to-Inference Closed Loop for Full-Precision 1T-Class MoE Models on Consumer Hardware

title.en: KTransformers: The Fine-Tuning-to-Inference Closed Loop for Full-Precision 1T-Class MoE Models on Consumer Hardware
title.zh: KTransformers：消费级硬件上全精度万亿参数级 MoE 模型的微调到推理闭环

talks.originalAbstract:
Frontier open-source MoE models are entering the 1T-parameter era, traditionally requiring data center GPU clusters for adaptation and deployment. KTransformers offers a low-cost alternative for 4090-class workstations using CPU-GPU heterogeneous co-compute. By offloading sparse MoE experts to CPU DRAM while keeping hot dense computation on a 24GB-class GPU, KTransformers enables efficient local inference.

More than just an inference engine, this architecture supports a complete workstation-level iteration loop: serving the model locally, collecting domain-specific feedback, fine-tuning LoRA adapters via LLaMA-Factory, and deploying the adapted model back to KTransformers. This approach provides small applied AI teams, university labs, and researchers a practical, parameter-efficient path to study, serve, and iterate on 1T-class models without prohibitive hardware costs.

overview.en: KTransformers enables efficient local inference for 1T-class MoE models on consumer hardware by leveraging CPU-GPU heterogeneous computing. It supports a full fine-tuning-to-inference loop, allowing model serving, feedback collection, and deployment back to the system. This approach makes large-scale model iteration accessible to small teams and researchers without high hardware costs.
overview.zh: KTransformers 通过利用 CPU-GPU 异构计算，在消费级硬件上实现了 1T 级 MoE 模型的高效本地推理。它支持从微调到推理的完整闭环，允许模型服务、反馈收集和部署回系统。这种方法使小型团队和研究人员能够在不需高昂硬件成本的情况下研究、服务和迭代大型模型。

talks.originalTitle: Agentic AI on Global Edge: Deploying SPEAR-Powered Operations Agents with MCP

title.en: Agentic AI on Global Edge: Deploying SPEAR-Powered Operations Agents with MCP
title.zh: 全球边缘环境中的智能体 AI：借助 MCP 部署由 SPEAR 驱动的运维智能体

talks.originalAbstract:
As ByteDance’s global edge infrastructure scales, centralized operations struggle with latency and fragmented edge scenarios. We built lightweight AI operations agents natively on the SPEAR edge platform, leveraging its built-in AI capabilities and native MCP support to rapidly ship purpose-built agents.
Deployed locally on edge nodes, these agents autonomously handle real-time cluster monitoring, root cause analysis and automated issue resolution without relying on central services, drastically cutting response latency and manual overhead.
In this talk, we deep-dive into SPEAR’s edge AI runtime architecture, MCP-enabled agent development patterns, and key engineering lessons from our global production rollout, including edge resource optimization and network resilience practices.

overview.en: ByteDance's global edge infrastructure faces challenges with centralized operations due to latency and fragmented scenarios. By deploying lightweight AI operations agents on the SPEAR platform with MCP support, they achieve real-time monitoring, root cause analysis, and automated resolution at the edge, reducing latency and manual effort. The talk covers SPEAR's edge AI architecture, MCP-based agent development, and production insights on resource optimization and network resilience.
overview.zh: 字节跳动的全球边缘基础设施面临集中式运维带来的延迟和场景碎片化问题。通过在 SPEAR 平台部署支持 MCP 的轻量级 AI 运维智能体，可在边缘端实现实时监控、根因分析和自动化处置，降低延迟与人工成本。本次演讲将介绍 SPEAR 的边缘 AI 运行架构、基于 MCP 的智能体开发模式，以及全球生产部署中的资源优化与网络韧性实践。

talks.originalTitle: DHttp: From Partial Connectivity to Omniconnectivity

title.en: DHttp: From Partial Connectivity to Omniconnectivity
title.zh: DHttp：从部分连接到全域互联

talks.originalAbstract: 智能体互联网时代，为什么需要新的互联网，传统的万维网又有哪些缺陷？回顾互联网的发展史，会发现传输层以下都是公平的——任何一个网络设备都有 IP 地址、MAC 地址，每个不同的软件和硬件都被平等地对待；然而到了应用层，就不公平了：域名并非任意设备都能拥有，DNS 仅服务于数据中心网络环境中的节点，这对移动网络、家庭网络中的边缘智能体一点都不公平！而这一切在万维网的 HTTP 协议提出来之时就注定了，服务端上升到云端，客户端下沉到边缘，两者从一出生阶级差异就存在了。然而，谁说边缘 AI 不是服务端呢？Agent 要调用的工具、数据和设备，往往不在云上，而在用户身边。DHttp 协议正是为了破解这一难题，为阶级平等而来。DHttp 并不是重新发明 Http，而是在QUIC 和 HTTP3 的基础上实现了点到点通信、端到端加密，扩展 DNS 协议使其支持泛端点网络地址，进而融合客户端与服务端为一体，客户端即服务端，让域名、私钥、证书这套完美的 TLS 身份普适化到任何一个边缘 AI 上。它们产生了奇妙的组合反应，天然具备身份认证、安全传输、数据完整性，轻松解决了通过堆砌冗杂设计才解决的一系列难题。DHttp 将为我们揭开两两之间皆可互连的“真互联”世界的帷幕，开启万智互联全新体验！

overview.en: DHttp addresses the limitations of traditional HTTP by enabling peer-to-peer communication and end-to-end encryption. It extends DNS to support universal endpoint addresses, allowing edge AI devices to act as both clients and servers, achieving true equality in network interactions. This protocol simplifies secure, identity-based communication across diverse networks, paving the way for a more interconnected future.
overview.zh: DHttp 解决了传统 HTTP 的局限性，实现了点对点通信和端到端加密。它扩展了 DNS 以支持泛端点网络地址，使边缘 AI 设备能够同时作为客户端和服务端，实现网络交互的真正平等。该协议通过简化安全、基于身份的通信，解决了复杂设计带来的诸多问题，为万物互联的未来铺平道路。

talks.originalTitle: OpenCV 5: What’s New—and How to Prepare Your Company for the Upgrade

title.en: OpenCV 5: What’s New—and How to Prepare Your Company for the Upgrade
title.zh: OpenCV 5：有哪些新变化，以及企业应如何为升级做好准备

talks.originalAbstract:
OpenCV 5 is the most consequential modernization of the world’s leading open-source computer vision library in years. This talk explains what changed, why it matters, and how engineering leaders can upgrade without disrupting production systems.

We will tour the new foundation—C++17 and Python 3 baselines, removal of legacy APIs, expanded data types, true 0D/1D arrays, and the reorganization of features, geometry, calibration, stereo, and point-cloud capabilities. We will then examine the radically revised DNN stack: a new inference engine with much broader modern ONNX support, dynamic shapes and subgraphs, optional ONNX Runtime integration, stronger CPU performance, and end-to-end building blocks for vision-language models. We will also highlight modern local features and matching, improved robust estimation, multi-camera calibration, and new 3D workflows.

The second half is a practical migration playbook for companies. Attendees will learn how to inventory dependencies, identify removed or relocated APIs, convert legacy Caffe and Darknet models to ONNX, benchmark CPU and GPU execution paths, build compatibility tests, run OpenCV 4 and 5 in parallel, stage deployment, monitor regressions, and preserve a rollback path. You will leave with a concrete checklist for deciding when to upgrade and reducing technical, operational, and organizational risk.

overview.en: OpenCV 5 represents a major modernization of the leading open-source computer vision library, introducing updates to its foundation, DNN stack, and local features. The talk provides a practical guide for companies to upgrade smoothly, including migration strategies and risk mitigation.
overview.zh: OpenCV 5 是近年来对领先开源计算机视觉库的重大现代化更新，包含基础架构、深度学习栈和局部特征的改进。本次演讲为公司提供了一套实用的升级指南，涵盖迁移策略和风险缓解方法。

talks.originalTitle: RustNN at the Edge: WebNN as Infrastructure for Local AI Agents

title.en: RustNN at the Edge: WebNN as Infrastructure for Local AI Agents
title.zh: 边缘端 RustNN：以 WebNN 作为本地 AI 智能体的基础设施

talks.originalAbstract:
AI agents promise autonomy, but today they are tethered to the cloud. Local inference is the bottleneck. Every agent needs to run
 models on whatever device the user has, and building that support from scratch is prohibitively expensive. RustNN and the W3C
 WebNN standard offer a practical solution: a single graph builder with an operator set designed to run on as many platforms as
 possible, from ONNX Runtime and CoreML to LiteRT and beyond.

 This talk shows what the RustNN ecosystem delivers today. We will cover the RustNN API and how it enables writing an ML workload
 once in Rust and running it in three environments: as a native application on your desktop, as a Node.js addon in a server or
 local process, or as a compiled WebAssembly module in a browser. All three share the same RustNN/WebNN runtime without forking
 the codebase. We will show how WebNN graphs are defined and executed in Rust, and how the same code hits hardware acceleration
 whether it is running on your desktop GPU, inside Node.js, or in a browser WebNN backend. Finally, we will discuss where the
 project is headed.

overview.en: RustNN and the W3C WebNN standard provide a unified solution for running AI agents locally. The RustNN ecosystem allows developers to write ML workloads once in Rust and deploy them across three environments: desktop, Node.js, and WebAssembly. This approach enables hardware acceleration across different platforms without code duplication.
overview.zh: RustNN 和 W3C WebNN 标准为本地运行 AI 智能体提供了统一的解决方案。RustNN 生态系统允许开发者在 Rust 中编写一次机器学习任务，并部署到桌面、Node.js 和 WebAssembly 三种环境中。这种方法可以在不同平台实现硬件加速，而无需代码重复。

talks.originalTitle: From Khronos AI Ecosystem Research Insights to Edge AI Inference with Vulkan

title.en: From Khronos AI Ecosystem Research Insights to Edge AI Inference with Vulkan
title.zh: 从 Khronos AI 生态研究洞察到基于 Vulkan 的边缘 AI 推理

talks.originalAbstract: As AI and real-time graphics continue to converge, portable AI inference is shifting from research to real-world deployment. This presentation explores insights from the Khronos AI Ecosystem Research Project, the open-source frameworks enabling AI inference using Vulkan today, and emerging trends in machine learning and neural graphics. We’ll show selected use cases where Vulkan-based AI inference is a strong fit, including texture compression, LLM inference, image upscaling, and frame interpolation.

overview.en: As AI and real-time graphics converge, portable AI inference is transitioning from research to real-world deployment. This talk presents insights from the Khronos AI Ecosystem Research Project, open-source frameworks for Vulkan-based AI inference, and emerging trends in machine learning and neural graphics. Use cases such as texture compression, LLM inference, image upscaling, and frame interpolation are highlighted.
overview.zh: 随着AI与实时图形技术的融合，便携式AI推理正从研究转向实际部署。本次演讲介绍了Khronos AI生态系统研究项目的关键洞察，以及当前基于Vulkan的AI推理开源框架和机器学习、神经图形领域的新兴趋势。展示了纹理压缩、LLM推理、图像超分和帧插值等适用Vulkan AI推理的典型应用场景。
